STYLE AND CONTINUITY LOCK: Preserve the supplied illustration identities, proportions, clothing, coherent anatomy, ink outlines, fine crosshatching, stable paper texture, teal night and amber highlights throughout. One continuous shot, no cuts, no morphing, no new text or speech bubbles, no lip-sync or audible dialogue. Keep all established subjects recognizable and in frame. No humans transform into monsters. Motion is natural within the illustrated world.
First half-second quiet lead-in. Harper initially watches the departing monsters offscreen RIGHT while the boy already looks up at her. At 1 to 2.8 seconds she gradually turns her head and eyes down toward the boy and gives one restrained reassuring small smile. He meets her gaze with quiet delighted disbelief, a tiny eyebrow lift and small smile, hugging his sketchbook. At 3.5 to 5.5 seconds they turn their attention back toward the creatures offscreen RIGHT together. Remaining seconds watch the departures, breathe naturally, slight hair movement. Harper is a grounded professional, never cutesy or coy: no wink, giggle, exaggerated head tilt, hand flourish or bobbing. Lips closed, no speech, no touching. Camera imperceptibly eases backward, only 3 percent wider across whole take.
purpose: User-approved reprise/outro plan, 12-frame lead-in and best-part selection.
